Call Activity

General Concept: A Call Activity in BPMN is used to invoke a separate process (subprocess) from within the current process. It allows for process reuse and modular design, letting you call a reusable workflow as part of a larger process.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Call Activity triggers the execution of another BPMN process definition. You can pass input variables to the called process and receive output variables when it completes. Input and output mappings are defined using FEEL expressions, allowing flexible data transformation. Variable scoping ensures that variables in the called process do not overwrite those in the parent process unless explicitly mapped. TaktX supports synchronous and asynchronous invocation, and handles subprocess lifecycle, error propagation, and boundary events attached to the Call Activity.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Call Activity in TaktX allows you to:

  • Invoke reusable subprocesses, passing input and receiving output variables.
  • Define input and output mappings using FEEL expressions for flexible data transformation.
  • Choose synchronous or asynchronous invocation of subprocesses.
  • Configure error handling, retries, and compensation for subprocess execution.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.

 

Example: Customer Onboarding with Call Activity

 

This example shows a process where a Call Activity invokes a reusable subprocess for customer onboarding. The Call Activity demonstrates modular process design and reuse of common workflows.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use input/output mappings to control which data is passed between parent and called process.
  • Design called processes to be reusable and independent.
  • Attach boundary events to handle errors or timeouts in the called process.
  • Use FEEL expressions for advanced data mapping and transformation.

Pitfalls:

  • Be careful with variable scoping—unmapped variables will not be visible in the called process.
  • Ensure the called process exists and is deployed in TaktX.
  • Handle errors and exceptions from the called process to avoid unexpected process termination
